content: The World Medical Association (WMA) is an international organization composed of physicians. It was officially established on September 17, 1947, following the resolutions adopted during the First General Assembly of the WMA, which took place in Paris, France. By 2007, the WMA had a membership comprising 84 national medical associations, collectively representing approximately 9 million physicians worldwide. The mission of the World Medical Association is to serve humanity by striving to achieve the highest international standards in medical education, scientific research, medical ethics, and healthcare delivery for all people across the globe. In October 2007, Yoram Blachar, an Israeli physician, was elected as the president of the World Medical Association. At the time of his election, Blachar was 67 years old and had been serving as the chairman of the Israel Medical Association since 1995. Blachar expressed his intention to work towards including African and Arab countries that were not yet members of the organization.
